I have tried to describe not only what was proposed, but why these ideas felt compelling at the time, why confidence rose and fell, and how later evidence changed our sense of what could count as an explanation.

papers.title: Resonance-aware NLOPS matching for off-shell $t\bar t+tW$ production in association with a Higgs boson
papers.abstract: We present a new NLO QCD Monte Carlo generator for the complete off-shell final state encompassing $t\bar tH$ and $tWH$ production with dileptonic decays, matched to parton showers in the resonance-aware POWHEG-RES framework. At Born level the calculation corresponds to the process $pp\to b\bar b\,e^+ν_e\,μ^-\barν_μ\,H$ in the four-flavour scheme with massive $b$ quarks. The complete matrix elements include all double-resonant, single-resonant and non-resonant topologies, all interferences and spin correlations, with both top quarks and $W$ bosons treated in the complex-mass scheme. This approach provides a unified and consistent treatment of $t\bar{t} H$ and $tWH$ production modes without the need for a diagram-removal or diagram-subtraction prescription. The generator, dubbed $\texttt{bb4lH}$, is implemented in the POWHEG-RES framework with OpenLoops amplitudes, and takes advantage of the multiple-radiation scheme ($\texttt{allrad}$) and of matrix-element-based resonance projectors. Semileptonic events are also supported and can be obtained from dileptonic ones, including QCD radiation in the hadronic $W$-boson decay. In addition, we present two new on-shell POWHEG generators for $t\bar{t} H$ and $tWH$ production, the latter being the first of its kind. We validate all generators against known fixed-order results and in the narrow-width limit, and present NLO and NLOPS predictions for the LHC in the dileptonic and semileptonic channels. Tuned comparisons with the corresponding on-shell descriptions show good agreement for inclusive observables, while sizeable differences arise in observables sensitive to the reconstructed top-quark line shape and in $tWH$-enriched regions. These findings are of direct relevance for the LHC analysis of $t\bar{t} H$ events and for the separation of $t\bar{t} H$ and $tWH$ production.

papers.title: Simulation-based inference for gravitational-wave cosmology: parameter reconstruction of a first-order electroweak phase transition
papers.abstract: The detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) from a cosmological first- order phase transition would be unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model, with a strong electroweak phase transition (EWPT) at LISA as a prime example. Reconstructing the underlying model from such a signal is challenging, since the map from the model parameters to the spectrum is degenerate and strong transitions occupy only small and sparse regions of parameter space. We show that simulation-based inference (SBI), a likelihood-free approach applicable to generic SGWB sources, provides a reliable parameter reconstruction despite these difficulties. We first apply SBI to the thermodynamic parameters characterizing the transition, namely its strength, inverse duration, temperature and bubble wall velocity. As a concrete application, we then consider a strong EWPT in a singlet extension of the Standard Model and reconstruct the model parameters from the resulting SGWB. We find that the SBI posteriors agree with those of a likelihood-based Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis, at negligible cost per data set once the network has been trained. Using the network posterior as the proposal for importance sampling with the exact likelihood further corrects its remaining deviations, at a sampling efficiency several orders of magnitude higher than sampling from the prior. SBI thus offers a fast and flexible framework for the cosmological science case of LISA

papers.title: Dirac leptogenesis with charged leptons
papers.abstract: Popular frameworks that explain the baryon asymmetry of the Universe (BAU) are electroweak baryogenesis, requiring a first-order phase transition, and Majorana leptogenesis, which relies on lepton number violation in the neutrino sector. Dirac leptogenesis offers an alternative mechanism that avoids both requirements, instead allowing the BAU to follow from previously generated chiral asymmetries that remain out of equilibrium in the early Universe. Conventional realizations of this scenario typically invoke ultra-light Dirac neutrinos. In this work, we generalize the mechanism to include Standard Model charged leptons by assuming that their mass-generating interactions have a UV origin and arise from higher-dimensional operators. For concreteness, the analysis is performed within a Froggatt-Nielsen setup, which allows us to naturally address fermionic mass hierarchies, too, now linked to the BAU, and we show that the proposed mechanism is viable by supercooling the flavon phase transition. The framework predicts a flavon with a (1.7-50) GeV mass, bounded by the non-observation of lepton flavor violation and the requirement for the Universe to not reheat above sphaleron temperatures, which could be indirectly probed by future lepton flavor violation experiments.

papers.title: Automate the geometric SMEFT at dimension eight
papers.abstract: We present the first complete dimension-eight implementation of the geometric Standard Model Effective Field Theory (geoSMEFT) as UFO models for event generators such as MadGraph. The models contain all 674 baryon-number-conserving operators, with minimal flavour violation for the fermionic operators, and are also provided in the Murphy basis. We include dimension-six contributions and electroweak input-parameter corrections consistently through order $1/Λ^4$, and provide dimension-eight squared contributions as a diagnostic of EFT truncation. We validate the implementation against independent calculations and Ward identities. To make these models practical for collider studies, we develop a standalone tool that identifies all operators contributing to a given process at tree level, including those entering through input-parameter shifts. It reports their expected energy scaling and generates a restriction card to reduce the computational cost of event generation. The same geometric construction allows us to calculate two- and three-point functions beyond dimension eight, to arbitrary order in $1/Λ^2$. The models and the tool are publicly available.

papers.title: Scherk-Schwarz Compactifications: From Circles to Strings
papers.abstract: This review is written with a simple question in mind: what does one need to know to enter the literature on Scherk-Schwarz compactifications? It is organized as a sequence of questions that a graduate student might naturally ask, together with the concepts, calculations, and formal tools needed to work through the literature. The discussion starts at an elementary field-theory level and gradually develops toward more advanced aspects of supergravity, orbifolds, quantum effects, and string theory. Phenomenological applications are deliberately left aside.

papers.title: Theory of Particle Scattering on Superconducting Qubits: From Single Devices to Quantum Arrays
papers.abstract: Superconducting qubits provide microwave-scale transitions and thus offer quantum targets for direct particle scattering with extremely small energy transfer. We develop a general framework for inelastic scattering in which an incident particle exchanges an off-shell photon with a superconducting quantum circuit, inducing a transition from a lower-energy internal state of the circuit to a higher-energy one. The target dependence is encoded in a finite-momentum electromagnetic transition current and, for charge-dominated response, in a qubit transition form factor. A key feature of particle scattering is that a microwave-scale excitation does not necessarily correspond to a long-wavelength interaction, since nonrelativistic particles can transfer spatial momenta much larger than the deposited energy. The full finite-momentum device response is therefore essential. We specialize the formalism to transmon qubits, construct a realistic electrostatic response for a planar Xmon-style transmon, and apply it to photon-mediated scattering of eV-scale bosonic dark matter, including final-state Bose stimulation. We find that the resulting enhancement substantially improves the projected sensitivity at the lowest masses. Owing to the exceptionally low transition threshold of superconducting qubits, this approach opens sensitivity to dark matter in the eV-to-keV mass range, which remains largely unexplored by existing direct-detection experiments. We further show that $N$ independently operated qubits give the expected rate proportional to $N$, while suitably prepared Dicke states can in principle achieve a collective enhancement approaching $N^2$ when spatial coherence is maintained across the array. These results establish superconducting qubits as quantum targets for direct particle scattering and provide a framework for optimizing low-threshold dark-matter searches.

papers.title: Locally infrared finite two-loop amplitudes for multi Higgs production in association with one jet
papers.abstract: We study the two-loop amplitudes for multi-Higgs production through a massive top-quark loop in association with one jet. We consider the quark-antiquark channel with a final-state gluon, $q\bar q\to g+nH$ although our construction applies to crossed channel as well. We utilize (non-local in momentum space) Ward identities to factorize longitudinal and gauge degrees of freedom through exact identities between Feynman graphs without reference to an infrared region. In the genuine two loop topologies, we replace the internal gluons by their physical degrees of freedom and show that the resulting amplitude is free of collinear singularities. The only remaining infrared divergence is a soft singularity that can be identified with a change of reference gauge vector. We construct explicit soft counterterms for these singularities, obtaining a locally infrared-finite representation. We verify that the factorized longitudinal degrees of freedom reproduce the remaining infrared poles of the original Feynman graphs. Our formalism requires no counter-terms for collinear finiteness or for manifesting Ward identities in various regions since we perform a decomposition of covariant gauge Feynman graphs. We expect its extension to more complicated processes to eliminate all collinear singularities--particularly in the initial state.

papers.title: Nucleon light-front transverse densities from three-body and quark + diquark Faddeev equations
papers.abstract: Nucleon elastic electromagnetic form factors obtained from two complementary continuum Schwinger function approaches -- a Poincaré-covariant three-body Faddeev equation formulated in rainbow-ladder truncation and a quark + fully-interacting-diquark, $q(qq)$, Faddeev equation -- are used to chart light-front transverse charge and magnetisation densities of the proton, the neutron, and their dressed valence quarks. Going beyond a comparison of observables, the bound-state amplitudes that underlie them are also compared. Both amplitudes are dominated by $s$-wave structures; and in the three-body solution, the mixed-antisymmetric (mixed-symmetric) flavour component is dominated by structures with the Dirac character of scalar (axialvector) diquark correlations, so that the association between these flavour components and diquark correlations is realised explicitly. The $q(qq)$ amplitude falls more slowly with the quark-diquark relative momentum than the three-body amplitude does with the corresponding Jacobi momentum. The two descriptions deliver mutually compatible densities, which match expectations based on modern parametrisations of data. Transverse-plane valence $u$- and $d$-quark Dirac radii are practically indistinguishable, whereas the $d$-quark Pauli radius is roughly 10% larger; and the valence $d$ quark is magnetically far more active than the valence $u$ quark, a feature tied to the mixed-symmetric (axialvector-diquark) components of the nucleon amplitude. For a $+\hat{x}$ polarised nucleon, positive charge is displaced in the $+\hat{y}$ direction, with the opposite effect for negative charge.

papers.title: From geometric curvature to effective backgrounds: a dictionary for Dirac fermions in one, two and three spatial dimensions
papers.abstract: Dirac equation on curved backgrounds can be rewritten as a flat-space equation in which geometry appears as a tensorial Fermi velocity together with a set of background fields. We derive this correspondence from a single Clifford-algebra identity and follow it through one, two, and three spatial dimensions. Once the spin connection is written in terms of Ricci rotation coefficients, only two contractions can occur. The trace produces a term with the index structure of a vector potential in every dimensionality; it enters with an imaginary factor i and is precisely the term that keeps the operator Hermitian when the Fermi velocity depends on position. The totally antisymmetric contraction produces an object that depends on the number of indices available to the Levi-Civita symbol: a trace on a line, a pseudoscalar mass on a surface, and an axial vector potential in a volume. Neither contraction is invariant under local rotations of the frame, and we give the transformation laws. On a surface, the curl of the trace term can always be removed by a frame rotation, while its divergence is proportional to the Gaussian curvature. We apply the correspondence to a Gaussian bump, where the local density of states at the center falls below its flat value and obeys a closed form at low energy; to a wire, where a nonuniform lapse binds states inside the gap and a nonuniform velocity cannot; to stationary frames on a surface, where a circulating drag shifts the Dirac mass locally with either sign; and to twisted and rotating frames in a volume, where the axial term takes the form of a chiral chemical potential produced by the frame alone, or separates Weyl nodes in a rotating sample. We separate the geometric contribution from the lattice pseudogauge field that dominates the response of strained samples

papers.title: Three-nucleon potentials and their matrix elements for $δ_{\mathrm{NS}}$ in superallowed $β$ decays
papers.abstract: We derive three-nucleon potentials for radiative corrections at order $\mathcal{O}(αε_χ^2)$ in chiral effective field theory where $α$ is the electromagnetic coupling and $ε_χ$ is the chiral expansion parameter. These corrections contribute to the nuclear-structure-dependent term $δ_\mathrm{NS}$ for determinations of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix element $V_{ud}$ from superallowed nuclear $β$ decays. We compute matrix elements of three-nucleon contributions at orders $\mathcal{O}(α^2)$ and $\mathcal{O}(αε_χ^2)$ using quantum Monte Carlo methods. We find the matrix elements at order $\mathcal{O}(α^2)$ to be large and to have an effect on the extraction of $V_{ud}$ at the scale of $10^{-4}$. In the case of $^{10}$C, the matrix elements of $\mathcal{O}(αε_χ^2)$ three-nucleon operators provide a 2% correction to $δ_{\text{NS}}$, and are thus beyond the current precision goals. The relative size of three-nucleon corrections to $δ_{\text{NS}}$ in medium mass nuclei, where two-body contributions tend to be smaller, remains to be investigated. We then use these results to determine $V_{ud}$ from the superallowed transition ${}^{10}\mathrm{C}\rightarrow{}^{10}\mathrm{B}$.

papers.title: Pole parameters of the $f_2(1270)$ and $f_2'(1525)$ from a coupled-channel analysis of the radiative $J/ψ$ multipoles
papers.abstract: We determine the pole parameters of $f_2(1270)$ and $f_2'(1525)$ from the combined fit to the isoscalar $D$-wave $ππ$ phase shift, the $ππ\to K\bar K$ modulus, and the BESIII $J/ψ\toγπ^0π^0$ and $γK_SK_S$ data: all three $2^{++}$ multipoles $E1$, $M2$ and $E3$, and the $M2$-$E1$ phases. The hadronic amplitude is a two-channel $K$-matrix with two poles and all parameters free, so that no resonance information is taken from the Particle Data Group. The radiative decay amplitudes are written as a coupled-channel Muskhelishvili-Omnès representation, with the Omnès matrix generated by that hadronic amplitude. The left-hand cuts, which carry the production dynamics, are approximated by a linear subtraction polynomial in the physical region. The model-independent kinematic constraints among the $J=2$ helicity amplitudes are implemented explicitly. The fit describes all $358$ points with $χ^2/N=1.29$ and gives $\sqrt{s_p}=(1267.5\pm1.3\pm2.6)-i\,\frac{1}{2}\,(175.5\pm2.4\pm7.4)\ \mathrm{MeV}$ for the $f_2(1270)$ and $(1514.8\pm2.8\pm1.5)-i\,\frac{1}{2}\,(80.4\pm3.4\pm4.8)\ \mathrm{MeV}$ for the $f_2'(1525)$, where the first uncertainty is statistical, from a parametric bootstrap with the data errors rescaled by $\sqrt{χ^2/N}$ of each set, and the second systematic, from $17$ variations of the analysis.

papers.title: On the cosmic window for neutrino self-interactions
papers.abstract: Neutrino self-interactions ($ν$SI) beyond the Standard Model have arisen as a promising probe of new physics in cosmology. In this Letter, we show that $ν$SI emerging in the low-energy limit of renormalizable theories implies resonant mediator behavior. We identify two regions for $ν$SI: (i) neutrinos become tightly coupled with background evolution; for the first time, we establish how this evolution modifies the Boltzmann hierarchy equations (BHEs), and (ii) resonant $ν$SI dominates the dynamics with negligible background evolution, relevant for mediator masses $\sim 10^{-6}-1$ MeV. In region (i), before matter-radiation equality, neutrino free-streaming is determined by the effective four-fermion interaction, known as the heavy-mediator limit (HML); we explore the impact of background evolution on this scenario, and from our modified BHEs, we show that self-interacting dark radiation scenarios require larger couplings than previously estimated to mimic $ν$SI. Region (ii) shows that the simplest realization of $ν$SI mediated by a (pseudo)scalar particle leads to an extra radiation contribution of $ΔN_{\rm eff}^{\rm CMB} \approx 0$, instead of the commonly quoted $\simeq 0.12$, at the CMB epoch. Overall, we highlight that our findings should be considered in any plausible scenario involving $ν$SI.

papers.title: A New GUT
papers.abstract: We present a new class of 4-dimensional Grand Unified Theories where the gauge sectors of the standard model have a novel embedding in the unified group that does not factor through an $SU(5)$ subgroup. The smallest example has gauge algebra $\frak{su}(12)$ and an anomaly-free spectrum that produces the three standard model generations with no additional chiral matter. The embedding predicts the axion-photon anomaly ratio $E/N=2/3$ and the weak mixing angle $\sin^2θ_W=1/2$ at the unification scale. Gauge-mediated proton decay proceeds through flipped-$SU(5)$-like operators and the minimally charged smooth monopole carries two Dirac charge units. The global gauge group can be $SU(12)$ or $SU(12)/\mathbb{Z}_2$, with the former allowing color singlets of half-integer electric charge. We develop a GUT bootstrap to constrain $SU(n)$ embeddings with three generations and no additional chiral matter. For unified fermions in up to two-index representations, we prove that all new embeddings arise from the $SU(8m+4)$ family, including flavor unified models for $m \geq 2$.

papers.title: Light fermions can trigger a Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
papers.abstract: The Brout-Englert-Higgs effect produces the masses of the Standard Model particles. However, the cause of this effect is unknown. Beyond-the-Standard-Model theories aim to find the source of this effect, for example using a composite Higgs and dynamically generating its vacuum expectation value. In this paper, we show evidence from lattice simulations with vectorially coupled fermions and without Yukawa couplings that the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect could be triggered by the light masses of fermions. This suggests that an explanation entirely within the Standard Model could be possible. Moreover, our results are consistent with weak couplings and fermions can only impact the Higgs potential at NNLO. This implies a so far unidentified mechanism in an SU(2) scalar-fermion-gauge system that produces a non-zero vacuum expectation value. In addition, we find that the transition from a QCD-like behavior to a Higgs-like behavior happens when the fermion mass falls below twice the W/Z mass: a threshold that is integer valued but not connected to other critical physical behavior.

papers.title: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA stochastic constraints on first-order phase transitions: A tale of priors
papers.abstract: We re-examine the methodology for constraining cosmological first-order phase transitions from gravitational-wave searches using Bayesian statistical analysis. Specifically, we use results from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA searches for a stochastic gravitational wave background during observing runs O1--O4a. We explore multiple prior choices across three categories of fit parameters: geometrical parameters, thermodynamical parameters of phase transitions, and the parameters of an Abelian Higgs particle physics model. Our key finding is that the constraints on most parameters describing gravitational waves from a phase transition depend strongly on the prior. Consequently, the data do not yet allow to derive robust constraints on these parameters. Besides, even if a parameter is meaningfully constrained, the upper limit can vary significantly with the prior range. We provide practical recommendations for assessing the robustness of parameter estimates and guidelines for rigorously testing prior independence in future analyses.

papers.title: Instanton tunnelling as a verifiable benchmark for digital quantum simulation: circuit structure, classical simulability and hardware reproducibility
papers.abstract: We use instanton-mediated tunnelling in the quartic double well as a benchmark for digital quantum simulation that is checkable against an exact answer at every step. The instanton enters through the classical analysis; the hardware tests the dynamics of the lattice model. A unary (single-excitation) encoding maps N lattice sites to N qubits, with the single-excitation dynamics as a reference that remains classically cheap at any N. For a second-order Trotter circuit with adjacent, equal-angle XX/YY pairs on each bond, we prove that the Schmidt rank across any cut is at most four at every gate boundary and at most two after each pair, independently of N. Matrix-product-state simulations of this gate list reproduce the exact splitting up to N = 48. For this bond-wise formula the admissible Trotter step shrinks roughly as N^-2, so one tunnelling period costs about N^3.3 two-qubit gates; a kinetic/potential splitting keeps the step near 0.065 up to N=128, so this scaling belongs to splitting the kinetic term bond by bond. At a coarser, separately bounded step we measure the full transfer at N=8 on two superconducting processors, recovering the lattice splitting to a few percent and its dependence on the barrier height, which at this resolution is set by the lattice rather than by the instanton. Over 9 repetitions, runs taken minutes apart agree to shot noise, while runs hours to weeks apart differ by up to 6.1%, also on a fixed set of qubits; with sessions as the sampling unit, the processors differ in the damping, while a difference in the splitting is not established. Normalising by the measured single-excitation population extends the usable depth about 4-fold but does not improve the splitting. A Gaussian start state, which needs no diagonalisation, reproduces the splitting of the eigenvector-based start to within 1.6 percentage points.

papers.title: Radii of Sn Isotopes near the Proton Dripline from Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory
papers.abstract: We present the first $\textit{ab initio}$ lattice calculations of charge and matter radii of tin isotopes $^{96}$Sn, $^{98}$Sn, $^{100}$Sn, $^{102}$Sn and $^{104}$Sn near the proton dripline using nuclear lattice effective field theory with high-fidelity two- and three-nucleon forces combined with the partial-pinhole algorithm. The resulting radii are larger then predicted from other ab-initio methods. We find that variations of the three-nucleon interaction reveal substantial radius differences even among interactions with similar binding energies. We intensively discuss of the role of different choices of the three-body forces.

papers.title: Active Learning and Genetic Search for Discrete Abelian Flavor Model Building
papers.abstract: The sequential breaking of discrete flavor symmetries provides a theoretical framework that can explain quark mass and mixing angle hierarchies. Each model is identified by its field content, charge assignments and symmetry breaking pattern, leading to an enormous space of possible models; this motivates the investigation of computational approaches for identifying promising candidates. In this work, we focus on quark flavor models with the flavor symmetry group $G_F=(\mathbb{Z}_2)^p$, where $p$ is a positive integer; operators involving flavon fields which spontaneously break the flavor symmetry determine the size of the Yukawa matrix entries. We consider two search strategies: an active learning search employing a random forest regressor and a genetic search. The generation of candidate models is automated and models are evaluated using a loss function that takes into account the logarithmic discrepancy between the model prediction and target observable values as well as penalties for model complexity. We find that both our active learning and genetic algorithms significantly outperform random model generation, which we use as a control; our active learning approach identifies lower-loss models faster (i.e., with fewer exact model evaluations) than our genetic search, though each ultimately finds successful models. Our results support the effectiveness of active learning and evolutionary optimization as approaches to automate the search for promising models based on discrete flavor symmetries.

papers.title: Total Angular Momentum Assignments in the Hadron Spectrum
papers.abstract: Predicting the total angular momentum $J$ for hadronic resonances whose spins have not yet been experimentally determined constitutes an important step in the spectroscopy of observed hadrons. In the present study, we develop a data-driven model in order to predict the value of $ J $ for hadrons with unknown spins using a dataset of known mesons and baryons from the PDG, including information on their quark content, isospin, parity, mass and other spectroscopic features. In particular, we employ XGBoost classifiers along with nested optimization in order to discover spectroscopic patterns across different hadronic sectors. We also prepare a systematic list of hadrons with unknown or poorly determined values of $ J $, and study spin-parity assignments for those hadrons. Since the parity hypothesis is taken as an input to the model, our model predicts the value of $ J $ conditional on a given parity hypothesis rather than independently determining the full $J^P$ assignment. Our predictions for several theoretically studied states show good agreement with results from quark models, QCD sum rules, molecular models, and other phenomenological approaches, while predictions for some other states differ from existing theoretical assignments. These differences motivate further theoretical investigations and may be tested by future experimental measurements.

papers.title: Reproducing $J/ψ\to γ+3P$ data with meson spectroscopy and understanding $X(2370)$
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent BESIII claims that $X(2370)$ is a pseudoscalar glueball candidate, we reanalyze several radiative $J/ψ$ decays into three pseudoscalars, $J/ψ\toγPPP$, with emphasis on the $X(2370)$ region. A simultaneous analysis of the three invariant-mass projections in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0η^\prime$, including the pseudoscalar states $X(1835)$, $X(2120)$, $η(2225)$, $X(2370)$, $X(2500)$, and $η_c$, reproduces the observed dip near $2.2~\mathrm{GeV}$ and the enhancement near $2.4~\mathrm{GeV}$ through coherent interference, without invoking the additional broad $X(2800)$ component employed in the BESIII partial-wave analysis. We further analyze $J/ψ\toγπ^0π^0η$ and $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$ by including both pseudoscalar and axial-vector contributions, and show that multiple excited meson states collectively describe the data. The absence of a prominent $X(2370)$ signal in the $K^*(892)$ region can be understood from differing orbital angular-momentum requirements rather than flavor-singlet suppression alone. Our results indicate that $X(2370)$ is not exceptional compared with the other reported pseudoscalar states in this mass region. Therefore, interpreting $X(2370)$ as a glueball-dominated state should be treated with caution.

papers.title: Hadronic production of excited $B_c$ mesons at the LHC
papers.abstract: We study the hadronic production of ground-state and excited $B_c$ mesons at the LHC for $\sqrt{S}=13$ TeV within the framework of NRQCD factorization at leading order in QCD. The calculation includes the $1S$, $1P$, and $2S$ multiplets, with both color-singlet and color-octet contributions to direct $1P$ production. For $p_T>0.2$ GeV, the summed production cross section is $336.04^{+275.80}_{-175.43}$ nb; the quoted uncertainty combines the specified heavy-quark mass and common-scale variations and does not include PDF-set differences. The NNPDF3.0 and MSHT20LO predictions are approximately $23\%$--$24\%$ below the CT18LO result. With the adopted radiative-transition branching fractions, $2S$ feed-down increases the total $1P$ yield from $34.73$ to $75.34$ nb. The relative enhancement differs markedly among the four spectroscopic states, ranging from $38\%$ for $1^1P_1$ to $262\%$ for $1^3P_0$, and it reorders their integrated production hierarchy. Within the set of states included here, the ratio of the $1P$ yield to the inclusive ground-state yield increases from $0.103$ to $0.224$. We present the state-resolved distributions and the dependence of direct production on kinematic cuts, parton distributions, quark masses, and scale choices. These results illustrate the potential impact of $2S$ feed-down on the relative yields of the lowest $P$-wave $B_c$ states.

papers.title: Doubly heavy open--flavor tetraquarks within the relativistic quark model
papers.abstract: Mass spectra of the ground, orbitally and radially excited states of doubly heavy open--flavor tetraquarks are calculated within the relativistic quark model based on the quasipotential approach and quantum chromodynamics. Tetraquarks are considered as bound states of a heavy diquark $\mathrm{QQ^{\prime}}$ ($\mathrm{Q,Q^{\prime} = c,b}$) and a light antidiquark $\mathrm{\overline{qq^{\prime}}}$ ($\mathrm{q,q^{\prime} = u,d,s}$). The diquark--antidiquark interaction quasipotential includes both spin--independent and spin--dependent relativistic contributions. The finite sizes of the diquark and antidiquark are taken into account via the form factors of their interaction with gluons. Masses of the ground ($1S$) and excited ($1P$, $2S$, $1D$, $2P$, $3S$) states are calculated including the mixing of states with the same observable quantum numbers $J^{P}$ but different spins $S$. The obtained masses are compared with the lowest allowed thresholds for strong fall--apart decays into a pair of heavy--light mesons in $S$--wave. Most of the states lie significantly above these thresholds. However, several states, predominantly orbital excitations with large $J$, lie below or slightly above the corresponding thresholds and, thus, could be promising candidates for experimental observation. The number of such near--threshold states increases for tetraquarks containing bottom quarks. The predicted mass of the ground state of the $\mathrm{cc\overline{ud}}$ tetraquark with $J^{P}=1^{+}$ is consistent with the experimentally observed $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{cc}}(3875)^{+}$ state.

papers.title: Search for Heavy Charged Higgs Bosons in Boosted Top and Bottom Quark Final States at a 1.4 TeV Future Lepton Collider
papers.abstract: The discovery potential for heavy charged Higgs bosons $H^\pm$ decaying into a top-bottom quark pair is investigated at a future $e^+e^-$ collider operating at $\sqrt{s}=1.4~\mathrm{TeV}$. The study considers charged Higgs masses between 200 and 600 GeV within all four Yukawa types of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM). The boosted $tb$ final state is explored using complementary cut-based and machine-learning analyses based on boosted decision trees (BDT). The expected signal significance and sensitivity contours in the $(m_{H^\pm},\tanβ)$ plane are obtained for each Yukawa type. The resulting sensitivity extends to regions of the 2HDM parameter space beyond the projected reach of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC), demonstrating the complementary potential of a future high-energy lepton collider to probe heavy charged Higgs bosons.

papers.title: Improving Sensitivity to Rare Processes at the LHC with Geodesic-Aware Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Rare processes at the Large Hadron Collider often lead to final states with quarks, for which the dominant backgrounds contain the same reconstructed objects as the signal. The colour structure of the hard process, imprinted on the pattern of soft QCD radiation, carries information that is largely left unused by standard analyses. We introduce a geometric representation of this colour flow by mapping hadronic constituents onto the unit sphere through a modified inverse stereographic projection centred on a pair of jets selected as a colour-singlet resonance candidate. The jet separation defines a circular region whose interior and exterior are mapped to opposite hemispheres, allowing a graph neural network to exploit the resulting radiation pattern using geodesic distances. As a benchmark, we consider flavour-changing neutral interactions of the top quark with the Higgs boson at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$~TeV, through associated $tH$ production and $t\bar t$ production with one top quark undergoing a $t\to qH$ decay, where $q=u,c$, focusing on subsequent $H\to b\bar b$ and leptonically top quark decays in both channels. Relative to a baseline graph neural network operating in the $(η,φ)$ plane, the geodesic-aware network improves the expected 95\% confidence-level limits on $\mathrm{BR}(t\to uH)$ and $\mathrm{BR}(t\to cH)$ by about an order of magnitude, to $1.1\times10^{-4}$ and $8.3\times10^{-5}$ for an assumed integrated luminosity of $139~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$. The approach can also be applied to searches for other colour-singlet resonances decaying into quarks or gluons.

papers.title: Probing dimension-six SMEFT operators in heavy-quark sector at future muon collider
papers.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity to the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) operators which define the interactions of heavy-quarks with electroweak gauge bosons and with leptons via the process $μ^- μ^+ \rightarrow Wtb$, followed by leptonic W-boson decays, at a 10 TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of 10 ab$^{-1}$. Signal and background events are generated at leading order using MadGraph5aMC@NLO, interfaced with Pythia 8 for parton showering and hadronization, and passed through Delphes 3.5 for fast detector simulation. The 95% confidence level (C.L.) limits on nine Wilson coefficients are derived using a cut-based method for two $b$-tagging working points (70% and 90% efficiencies). These limits are significantly tighter than those currently reported by the CMS Collaboration; furthermore, these results highlight the advanced potential of a future high-energy muon collider to investigate new physics within the electroweak sector through precise measurements of heavy-quark interactions.

papers.title: Role of excited hyperons in $K^{*}Ξ$ production via $K^{-}N$ scattering
papers.abstract: We investigate the production mechanism of $K^-N\to K^*Ξ$ and the role of high-mass excited hyperons within an effective Lagrangian approach, using a combined fit to cross section and polarization data for $K^-p\to K^{*+}Ξ^-$. The model includes $s$- and $u$-channel exchanges of the ground-state $Λ$ and $Σ$ hyperons, together with $s$-channel contributions from $Λ(2325)$ and $Σ(2230)$. The pronounced near-threshold enhancement of the total cross section is driven mainly by these excited hyperons, whereas $u$-channel exchange dominates at backward angles at higher energies. Polarization results show that both the $K^*$ spin-density matrix elements and the $Ξ$ recoil polarization are sensitive to excited-hyperon contributions near threshold. Notably, the latter remains sensitive to interference involving excited-hyperon amplitudes even at higher energies. Moreover, with the same fitted parameters and no additional free parameters, the predicted cross sections for $K^-p\to K^{*0}Ξ^0$ and $K^-n\to K^{*0}Ξ^-$ agree well with available measurements. Finally, a Dalitz analysis of $K^-p \to K^{*+}Ξ^- \to KπΞ^-$, together with existing $KπΞ^-$ cross section data, indicates the feasibility of reconstructing $K^{*+}Ξ^-$ through this final state. These results suggest that $K^*Ξ$ production provides a valuable reaction channel for investigating high-mass excited hyperons and their hadronic couplings, and offers theoretical guidance for future experimental measurements.

papers.title: Geoneutrinos (and reactor neutrinos) do not visibly decay
papers.abstract: Neutrinos that decay on their way to a detector arrive depleted, more so at low energies, where time dilation lengthens their lifetime the least. Geoneutrinos---electron antineutrinos from the radioactive decay of uranium and thorium inside the Earth---have energies of a few MeV and travel up to the diameter of the Earth. We use them to test neutrino decay for the first time. We compute the geoneutrino signal at Borexino, KamLAND, SNO+, and JUNO for visible decay, in which the daughter neutrinos are themselves detected, and compare it against their published data. We find no evidence of decay that holds across Earth models. Combining the four experiments, we limit the decay $ν_1 \to ν_3$ in the inverted mass ordering at 90% C.L.: $τ_1/m_1 > 3.7 \times 10^{-9}$ s eV$^{-1}$ when the radiogenic power of the Earth is left free and $τ_1/m_1 > 4.4 \times 10^{-9}$ to $1.6 \times 10^{-8}$ s eV$^{-1}$ when it is taken from Earth models. With an Earth model assumed, the geoneutrinos set the limit; with the power free, the antineutrinos from nuclear reactors that the same experiments detect count as much as the geoneutrinos. These are the first terrestrial limits on the visible decay of $ν_1$.

papers.title: Precision Measurements of the Effective Leptonic Weak Mixing Angle at Hadron Colliders
papers.abstract: We review precision determinations of the effective leptonic weak mixing angle, $\sin^2θ^\ell_{\mathrm{eff}}$, from Drell-Yan angular asymmetries at the Tevatron and the LHC. As statistical uncertainties have dramatically decreased, parton distribution function (PDF) uncertainty now dominates the most precise hadron-collider results. We describe the angular observables, electroweak calculation schemes, and advanced methods such as replica reweighting and Hessian profiling, used to constrain PDFs directly from measured angular distributions. To identify the origin of differences between modern PDF sets (e.g., CT18, MSHT20, NNPDF) in the extracted mixing angle, we employ a simplified leading-order Z-pole calculation that separates quark-flavor production weights from quark-direction dilution. We demonstrate how these PDF-induced differences can be mitigated by incorporating complementary constraints from W/Z cross-section ratios and W-boson decay asymmetries. Furthermore, we discuss the requirements for a common reinterpretation and future combination of LHC measurements, highlighting how correlated PDF uncertainties limit the ultimate combined precision. Finally, we outline future prospects, including complementary measurements in $Z+b$ production and high-mass tests of the running $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ weak mixing angle.

papers.title: Gravitational Form Factors and Transverse Mechanical Structure of the Charged Kaon in a Two-Fock-Sector Light-Front Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We study the electromagnetic and gravitational form factors of the charged kaon in a light-front Hamiltonian model with coupled $|u\bar s\rangle$ and $|u\bar s g\rangle$ Fock sectors. We solve the coupled Hamiltonian in a longitudinal Jacobi and transverse harmonic-oscillator basis, with the interaction strength fixed by the kaon mass. The momentum form factors are extracted from $T^{++}$, while the stress form factors are obtained from the transverse shear projection of the QCD Belinfante energy-momentum tensor, including diagonal, sector-changing, and constrained-field contributions. The strange antiquark carries the largest fraction of the kaon's longitudinal momentum, whereas the gluon carries only $2.05\%$. Despite this small momentum fraction, the gluon contributes $42.4\%$ of $|D_K(0)|$, for which we obtain $D_K(0)=-2.03610$. The charge and transverse momentum radii are $0.5178\pm0.0278\,\mathrm{fm}$ and $0.3394\pm0.0113\,\mathrm{fm}$, respectively, with uncertainties estimated from mass and basis variations. We obtain the transverse mechanical distributions using two ultraviolet continuations of the directly calculated $D$ form factors beyond $Q^2=2\,\mathrm{GeV}^2$. Both continuations give positive pressure at small transverse distances and negative pressure at larger distances. The corresponding transverse mechanical radii are $0.4616\pm0.0130\,\mathrm{fm}$ and $0.4768\pm0.0132\,\mathrm{fm}$, both larger than the transverse momentum radius. The central pressure changes substantially between the two continuations, whereas the pressure zero and mechanical radii vary much less.

papers.title: Projected Sensitivity of a Differential Torsion Sensor for Tests of the Weak Equivalence Principle
papers.abstract: Tests of the weak equivalence principle (WEP) are among the most sensitive probes of new long-range, composition-dependent interactions beyond general relativity and the Standard Model. We evaluate the potential of a differential torsion sensor, which combines long mechanical coherence times with optical-cavity readout and common-mode rejection, for laboratory WEP tests and fifth-force searches. For a representative configuration based on an existing prototype, with Be-Ti test masses and 180 days of coherent integration, the projected noise-limited sensitivity to the Eötvös parameter is $η\simeq7.5\times10^{-16}$ and $2.4\times10^{-16}$ for signal modulation at 2 and 20 mHz, respectively, below current ground-based torsion-balance limits. For a baryon-coupled Yukawa interaction sourced by the Earth, the corresponding projected sensitivity to the coupling strength is $α\simeq3.1\times10^{-13}$ and $9.8\times10^{-14}$ for ranges $λ\gtrsim10^{7}$ m. We identify the modulation scheme, the material contrast, and the source geometry as the main factors that set the projected reach, and the control of systematic couplings as the main experimental requirement for attaining it. These results indicate that differential torsion sensors are a promising platform for future laboratory WEP tests.

papers.title: Long-lived linear slow roll near critical and spinodal points in soft-wall AdS/QCD
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate the real-time evolution of the chiral condensate near critical and spinodal points within soft-wall AdS/QCD, focusing primarily on the long-lived prethermalization stage, in contrast to the conventional early transients and late-time relaxation. While the quasi-steady nature of this stage has been previously identified, we demonstrate that it is intrinsically a continuous linear slow roll, fundamentally distinct from the asymptotic critical slowing down at late times. By showing that the bulk evolution adiabatically follows the boundary condensate on a slow configuration space, we analytically project the 5D partial differential equation onto a boundary first-order Ginzburg-Landau (GL) equation. We find that the long lifetime of this linear regime is protected by a ``double-zero'' condition: the simultaneous vanishing of the local potential gradient (suppressing the drift velocity) and curvature (suppressing the acceleration). This geometric flatness inherently emerges at the second-order point and both first-order spinodal endpoints. Crucially, this behavior is not a fine-tuned artifact, but a generic consequence of the effective potential landscape intrinsic to these phase-transition endpoints, persisting across a broad class of physically relevant initial conditions and temperature quenches. A local short-time expansion further relates the interval duration to the potential curvature and its higher-order derivatives, in good agreement with our numerical simulations. This work establishes a direct link between the local structure of phase-transition endpoints and the dynamical evolution of the long-lived intermediate stage of the condensate.

papers.title: Coupled-channel pole structure and bare-state mixing of bottom-strange heavy-quark spin partners
papers.abstract: Motivated by the observation of the $B_{s0}^*(5700)$ and the heavy-quark symmetry relations connecting the $DK$, $D^*K$, $\bar{B}K$, and $\bar B^*K$ systems, we investigate whether the same chiral dynamics can generate negative-parity partners dominated by the $\bar B_1K$ and $\bar B_2^*K$ components. We further examine how nearby bare bottom-strange states reshape the pole spectrum through coupled-channel mixing. Both the relevant $S$-wave scattering and the lower-lying $P$-wave decay channels are explicitly included in the coupled-channel calculation. In the absence of bare states, the interaction generates two negative-parity poles near $6.15$ GeV. Coupling the hadronic channels to the corresponding quark-model configurations leads to a richer two-pole structure in each sector, with the pole masses, widths, and channel residues governed by the interplay between the bare states and the hadronic dynamics. In particular, the inclusion of the bare states substantially increases the widths of the negative-parity poles with the larger $S$-wave molecular components. The resulting correlated patterns in the pole spectrum provide testable signatures for future studies of excited bottom-strange mesons.

papers.title: Unpolarized Generalized Parton Distributions of the Nucleon in a Covariant Quark-Diquark Approach
papers.abstract: We study the unpolarized generalized parton distributions (GPDs) of the nucleon in a covariant quark-diquark approach, in which both scalar and axial-vector diquarks are treated as composite subsystems. Motivated by previous form factor studies, we introduce a vertex correction based on the pion cloud picture as a first exploratory treatment of pion cloud effects at the GPD level, in order to improve the description of $E^q(ξ, x, t)$ and related magnetic observables. At the model input scale, only valence quarks are included. With the vertex correction, the electromagnetic form factors $G_{E, M}$ and the mass form factor $A$ obtained from the Mellin moments of the GPDs agree well with those obtained from direct calculations. The vertex correction brings the evolved charge weighted distribution $\sum{e^q E^q(ξ, x, t)}$ closer to the phenomenological parametrization. The correction shifts transverse strength from the central region toward the peripheral region, consistent with the long range character of the pion cloud contribution. The transverse structure results further suggest a harder longitudinal momentum distribution in the central region of the nucleon than in its periphery. Furthermore, the evolved real part of the proton Compton form factor, $\mathrm{Re} \mathcal{H}(ξ, t)$, has a reasonable magnitude and follows the main trend of the Quantum Deep Neural Networks (QDNN) extraction. In addition, $\mathrm{Re} \mathcal{H}$ may be more sensitive to the ERBL region than the other physical quantities calculated in this work.

papers.title: Hadron masses and pseudoscalar meson form factors in a Poincaré-invariant constituent quark model
papers.abstract: We study a Poincaré-invariant constituent quark model with pair, fine-structure, and finite-range three-quark interactions treated in the diagonalization. A fit of 20 parameters to 36 meson and 27 baryon masses gives an rms deviation of $6.85\,\mathrm{MeV}$, with the common offset fixed by a spectral condition. The same mass-fit wave functions give the elastic form factors of ten pseudoscalar mesons in the light-front impulse approximation with the Melosh rotation. The pion and charged-kaon radii are $0.407$ and $0.411\,\mathrm{fm}$, below the measured values. Unlike experiment, the kaon radius slightly exceeds the pion radius. Replacing the pion radial function by the normalized $S$-wave component of the $ρ$ raises its radius to $0.604\,\mathrm{fm}$, showing that hyperfine compression accounts for most of the deficit in the mean-square charge radius. With the light-quark size fixed by the pion, the $K^+$ and $K^0$ radii require strange-quark sizes that differ by $2.2$ standard deviations.

papers.title: Comment on "Exact, nonsingular black holes from a phantom DBI field as primordial dark matter"
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the metric and scalar configuration proposed in Ref.~[1] do not satisfy the complete set of field equations of the Dirac-Born-Infeld (DBI) field theory minimally coupled to general relativity on a radial domain containing the event horizon. The physical DBI branch for this gravitational setup terminates outside the event horizon. Thus, the proposed configuration does not describe a black hole solution of that theory.

papers.title: Cold Magnetized Quark Matter under Compact-Star Conditions
papers.abstract: We investigate the phase structure of cold magnetized two-flavor quark matter under compact-star conditions within a nonlocal chiral quark model with separable interactions. Electric charge neutrality and beta equilibrium are imposed in order to describe matter under realistic neutron-star conditions, while nonlocality is implemented through a Gaussian form factor. We find that low and moderate magnetic fields reduce the critical chemical potential for chiral symmetry restoration, signaling inverse magnetic catalysis. For stronger magnetic fields, the critical chemical potential becomes nearly independent of the magnetic field strength, Compared with the isospin-symmetric case, the combined effects of charge neutrality and beta equilibrium shift the first-order chiral transition to slightly higher chemical potentials, indicating that compact-star constraints delay the onset of chiral symmetry restoration. We further show that charge neutrality and beta equilibrium modify the de Haas--van Alphen oscillations in the quark density, shifting the Landau-level thresholds for the $u$ and $d$ quarks in opposite directions relative to the isospin-symmetric case. The effect on the chiral transition is small ($\sim 5$MeV) for fields $B\lesssim 10^{19}$G, relevant for magnetar interiors, and becomes sizable only for $B\gtrsim 3\times10^{19}$G. These results highlight the importance of incorporating realistic stellar conditions in studies of the QCD phase diagram at high baryon density.

papers.title: Fuzzy Dark Matter as a diffractive barrier: Wave-optics Signatures of Ultralight Fields on Lensed Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) propagate through the universe from sources at high redshift, experiencing the gravitational fields of the intervening matter distribution. Halos composed of ultralight dark matter (ULDM) contain strong density fluctuations, reflecting the interference pattern in the field distribution of the ultralight bosons. In the wave-optics regime, ULDM fluctuations act as a diffractive grating, imprinting frequency-dependent modulations of GWs, in addition to magnification and other gravitational lensing effects. Since lensing depends on the projected surface density, we derive its approximate probability distribution and show how it departs from a Gaussian distribution depending on the halo profile and coherence length. We then quantify how the GW diffraction signatures produced by the granules depend on macroimage magnification and parity. The ULDM interference network imprints stochastic diffraction fluctuations at the $O(1)\%$ level on GWs moderately lensed by the host when the Fresnel scale is comparable to the granule coherence length $r_F(f)\sim\ell_c$. These fluctuations can be enhanced to $\gtrsim10\%$ when the host macroimage forms near the critical curve or for Type II macroimages. For massive black hole binaries observed by LISA, the diffraction signature can be detectable around the ULDM particle mass $m_φ\sim10^{-21}$ eV, providing either a smoking-gun signature of ULDM or new constraints on $m_φ$.

papers.title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
papers.abstract: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $ζ_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.

papers.title: The production of lepton pairs in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC energies
papers.abstract: We perform a quantitative study of dilepton production and elliptic flow in In+In collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=17.3$ GeV and isobar collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV, concentrating on the low and intermediate invariant mass regions. The medium evolution is simulated event-by-event with the multistage iEBE-MUSIC framework, and the electromagnetic emission combines for the first time quark-gluon plasma (QGP) emission calculated at next-to-leading order (NLO) in the strong coupling with in-medium radiation calculated with hadronic many-body theory. Freeze-out and surviving primordial $ρ$ decays are also included. The calculations are compared with the high-precision dimuon spectra measured by the NA60 Collaboration, and with STAR preliminary measurements of dielectron spectra and elliptic flow. We obtain effective temperatures extracted from the transverse-mass spectra, and we calculate the elliptic flow of the different dilepton sources. Our results suggest that dilepton measurements in the low-mass and high $p_T$ region can provide insight into higher-order corrections to the QGP emission rate.

papers.title: Twist-4 QCD Factorization for One-Point Correlators at Next-to-Leading Order in Electron-Ion Collisions
papers.abstract: Energy and charge correlators have emerged as powerful, infrared- and collinear-safe (IRC-safe) observables for probing QCD dynamics in the vacuum, established within the leading-twist factorization formalism. However, their IRC safety and factorization properties in a nuclear medium, where higher-twist contributions are critically enhanced, remain unproven. In this letter, we present the first proof of next-to-leading order QCD factorization for one-point energy and charge correlators (OPEC and OPCC) in electron-ion collisions at twist-4. Working within the higher-twist expansion framework, we calculate the twist-4 power corrections to the angular widths of the OPEC and OPCC, and explicitly demonstrate that the IRC singularities cancel and fragmentation-function dependence reduces to momentum and charge moments for final-state medium-enhanced observables in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering. Supported by numerical evaluations, this framework establishes OPEC and OPCC angular widths as sensitive probes of higher-twist dynamics and fundamental properties of cold nuclear matter.

papers.title: Capturing Ultralight Dark Matter Around Black Holes
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter (DM) can form hydrogen-like bound states around black holes (BHs), that can be perturbatively described at small gravitational fine-structure constant alpha=G*M*mu<<1, where M and mu are the masses of the BH and the DM scalar, respectively. We show that self-interactions lead to the formation of a 2p-halo around a Schwarzschild BH, with the final cloud density as high as 10^5 times the background density. We also show that for the case of a Kerr BH with a superradiant cloud, the decay of the 211 state can populate the ground state faster than it decays into the BH. Consequently, the 211 cloud mass is bounded from above by M_{211}^{crit}/M~=5*10^{-3}*alpha^{-1/2}*[f_a/10^{16} GeV]^2 up to an O(1) factor depending on the spin of the BH. Crucially, for rapidly spinning BHs with M~<4*10^6 M_{sun}, alpha~<0.03, and f_a~<9*10^{15} GeV the resulting superradiant cloud mass is lower than previously assumed, which might have an impact on axion bounds from measurements of stellar BH spins.

papers.title: Seeing through the fog: astrophysical priors and the evidence for new physics in pulsar timing arrays
papers.abstract: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) have found evidence for a gravitational wave background at nHz frequencies. Inspiralling supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs) likely contribute to at least part of the signal, but there may be additional cosmological sources from new physics in the early universe. Disentangling the two is complicated by the prohibitively slow modelling of SMBHB spectra based on realistic population models. Here we introduce binaryfog, a surrogate of up-to-date population models also used by the NANOGrav collaboration, that returns the statistical distribution of bent spectra $\mathcal{O}(10^6)$ faster than direct computation. We use binaryfog to profile over the six astrophysical parameters in fits of four extensively discussed new-physics models: a dark sector phase transition, cosmic superstrings, inflationary gravitational waves, and domain walls. Compared to the widely adopted power-law description of the SMBHB background, the preference for a phase transition drops from $2.8σ$ to $1.5σ$. The other three models follow a similar pattern. We also recommend updated astrophysical priors based on galaxy surveys published since 2014, which for current PTA data still only give a marginal preference of $1.7σ$ for a phase transition. An interpretation of the signal in terms of SMBHBs alone favours binaries that merge within about $2\,$Gyr after their host galaxies have merged, requiring an efficient mechanism to overcome the final parsec of separation. If binaries need longer than about $6.5\,$Gyr to merge, the preference for a phase transition exceeds $3σ$ under our recommended updated prior set. binaryfog can help resolve these questions, as it allows users to study the impact of updated astrophysical priors and a realistic SMBHB population model on new-physics searches with PTAs.

papers.title: The Price of Discovery: Cost-Optimized Detectors for the GUT-Scale QCD Axion
papers.abstract: Grand unification and string theory point to a quantum chromodynamics (QCD) axion with mass between $10^{-11}$ and $10^{-8}$ eV, while heterotic string theory suggests a mass of $0.5-0.8$ neV. We study which laboratory experiment could discover or exclude DFSZ-strength QCD axion dark matter at and above 0.5 neV at the lowest cost, which we estimate from scaling laws calibrated to historical data. We find that a lumped-element detector, building on the ABRACADABRA concept, can do so with demonstrated readout technology; an example is a shielded toroid about 14 m across with a 6 T NbTi magnet, whose magnet and cryostat we estimate at around 120 million Swiss francs (MCHF). If projected readout targets are met, a 5 m toroid at 25 MCHF suffices. We find these designs by optimizing the toroid, solenoid, and core lumped-element topologies under a common cost metric. The toroid emerges as the most promising and cost-effective topology. The optimal field of the toroid detector is far below the 16 T of the proposed DMRadio-GUT design, which would cost nearly twice as much as our optimum. Heterodyne searches with superconducting radio-frequency cavities, with cavity shapes that we optimize for price, cost between about the same as and twice as much as the lumped-element detectors, but require cavities of volumes $\sim50-2000$ m$^3$. We find that nuclear-magnetic-resonance searches (CASPEr) need orders-of-magnitude gains in spin polarization and coherence. We release axionMultiPhysics, an open-source finite-element and multiphysics package for, e.g., magnetoquasistatic and full-wave electromagnetics, superconductors, readout circuits, and mechanics, from which most of our numerical results were obtained.

papers.title: Why supersonic UAP events are not accompanied by acoustic booms?
papers.abstract: The Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) events have been recorded for decades. However, the nature of these events remains unknown. We advocate an idea that the dark matter (DM) in form of the axion quark nuggets (AQN) made of standard model quarks (or {\it antiquarks}) and gluons could {\it simultaneously} explain many observed puzzling features which always accompany the UAP events, such as high velocity, enormous acceleration, absence of any remaining materials in affected area, etc. This long list of mysterious features also includes the absence of any sound which normally accompanies any supersonic motion. The AQN framework answers this last puzzle as well, which represents the title of the present work. The AQN dark matter model was invented long ago without any intension to apply the model to UAP events. Rather, it was invented with a single motivation to explain the observed similarity $Ω_{\rm DM}\sim Ω_{\rm visible}$ between visible and DM components, which represents a very generic feature of this framework, not sensitive to any parameters of the construction. In this work we use the same framework with the same set of parameters to study the observed UAP events. Essentially we argue that a specific class of UAP represents the close cousin of other mysteries known for decades (even centuries), such as sky-quakes, Ball Lightnings, and Mysterious Transient events. In other words, the UAPs represent different manifestations of exactly the same objects, the AQNs propagating in atmosphere. The fuel powering all these mysterious energetic events is one and the same: it is the antiquark core of the AQNs. We also present some suggestions on type of instruments required to study this specific (and well defined) type of the UAP events.

papers.title: Steerability in top quark decays at the LHC
papers.abstract: Quantum information observables in top quark pair production have opened a new experimental window on non-classical correlations of particle interactions at colliders. Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) steering occupies a distinguished place in the quantum hierarchy, lying between entanglement and Bell nonlocality. We present a detailed collider analysis of steerability for top quark pairs at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). In particular, we utilize both the decay and kinematic methods to estimate the expected sensitivity of the LHC and High Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) to detect steerable states. We find that with the current LHC dataset of $139~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ the steerability of the $t\bar t$ state in the boosted region can be established at $7.7σ$ ($1.8σ$) in the semileptonic (dileptonic) channel with the decay method, corresponding to a measurement of the steerability integral at a precision of $1.5\%$ ($5.2\%$), while the kinematic method reaches a precision of $0.05\%$ in both channels. At the HL-LHC the decay-method precision improves to $0.3\%$ ($1.1\%$). Near threshold, where the inclusive selections used for entanglement and discord yield a state at the steerability boundary, an optimized selection $M_{t\bar{t}}\lesssim360$--$400$~GeV isolates a steerable singlet-dominated state, where the sensitivity is projected to reach $7σ$ ($3.4σ$). We also provide a detailed discussion on the interpretation of these results with respect to fictitious quantum states, and argue for the robust nature of the steerability measurement at colliders.

papers.title: Complete Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-handed Neutrino Loops
papers.abstract: We study the complete cosmological collider (CC) signatures from right-handed neutrino loops with chemical-potential enhancement. These CC signals are induced by the inflaton-right-handed-neutrino interaction and can be extracted in the collinear squeezed configuration, which allows the right-handed-neutrino triangle loop to be factorized into the hard and soft parts. We precisely compute the soft part of the fermion loop for the first time by using the complete mode functions and the full loop integral, and treat the hard part as a tree-level subdiagram. We subtract the large-momentum asymptotic terms of the soft loop integrand and retain their finite contributions to the oscillation. We then evaluate the full spinor-helicity and Schwinger-Keldysh sums to obtain a finite, closed analytic formula for the complex clock coefficient. We further derive a compact formula for the leading CC signals in the large-chemical-potential expansion. We analyze the structure of the soft-part contribution by examining the sum of residues of the Mellin poles of the fermion propagators. For this, we demonstrate that the first local pole on each soft line contributes half of the asymptotic coefficient on one Schwinger-Keldysh path and the remaining local poles on the second soft line supply the other half.

papers.title: Bayesian Multimessenger Constraints on Self-Bound Quark Stars in Revised Perturbative QCD
papers.abstract: We perform a Bayesian multimessenger analysis of self-bound two-flavor $ud$ quark matter described by a thermodynamically consistent revised perturbative-QCD equation of state (EOS), incorporating the GW170817 tidal information, mass--radius measurements, and pulsar mass constraints. The resulting posterior medians and $68\%$ credible intervals are $B_0^{1/4}=137.66^{+1.72}_{-1.86}\,\mathrm{MeV}$, $M_{\max}=2.166^{+0.035}_{-0.036}\,M_\odot$, $R_{1.4}=11.778^{+0.203}_{-0.196}\,\mathrm{km}$, and $Λ_{1.4}=768^{+90}_{-81}$. The posterior-predictive support probability for interpreting the $2.59\,M_\odot$ GW190814 secondary as a self-bound $ud$ quark star is of order $10^{-5}$, strongly disfavoring this interpretation within the adopted EOS framework. The reconstructed EOS exhibits characteristic self-bound behavior, with finite energy and baryon number densities at the zero-pressure surface and a median surface energy density of $ε_{\rm surf}\simeq187\,\mathrm{MeV\,fm^{-3}}$. Its pressure is suppressed relative to both the noninteracting $ud+e$ gas and the representative MIT bag-model prediction. Although the running strong coupling decreases with increasing quark chemical potential, its central value in maximum-mass configurations correlates positively with $M_{\max}$, indicating stronger coupling and reduced perturbative reliability toward the high-mass end. Notably, the squared speed of sound remains nearly constant, varying from $c_s^2\simeq0.321$ to $0.324$ between canonical and maximum-mass configurations, whereas the conformal measure $Δ=1/3-P/ε$ decreases substantially from approximately $0.208$ to $0.076$. This demonstrates that an approximately constant sound speed does not necessarily imply approximate conformality. The relativistic adiabatic index also increases sharply near the zero-pressure surface, reflecting the self-bound nature of the EOS.

papers.title: Electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks in a coupled-channel unitary approach
papers.abstract: We study the electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks $P_c(4312)$, $P_c(4440)$ and $P_c(4457)$ and of their four heavy-quark spin partners, treated as $\bar D^{(*)}Σ_c^{(*)}$ hadronic molecules. The states are poles of a coupled-channel unitary amplitude with a vector-meson exchange kernel that respects heavy-quark spin symmetry. The form factors are the residues at the double pole of the photon-coupled amplitude. The current consists of one-body currents and a photon--four-hadron vertex, which we construct for this channel space. Its gauged-kernel part ensures the charge normalization through the compositeness sum rule, while its contact parts contain couplings that the model does not determine. For $J^P=\tfrac12^-$, $\tfrac12^-$, $\tfrac32^-$ and pointlike constituents, the mean squared distances between the constituents of the three observed states are $0.85-0.47i$, $0.35-0.18i$ and $1.76-0.57i\,\mathrm{fm}^2$. Within $2\%$, they equal the zero-range value $1/(4μ_{\rm red} B_c)$, with reduced mass $μ_{\rm red}$ and complex binding energy $B_c$, times the effective-range factor of the amplitude. The real parts of the magnetic moments are $1.7$, $-0.9$ and $1.3\,μ_N$, within $11\%$ of the additive moments of the constituents. Variations of the constituent moments and of the magnetic contact couplings within bounds from dimensional analysis give the ranges $0.8$ to $2.0$, $-1.3$ to $-0.2$ and $0.2$ to $1.8\,μ_N$. The charge radii depend also on the constituent structure and on electric contact currents. The photon loops of open channels have a triangle singularity at spacelike momentum transfer. We specify the analytic continuation of the residue in $Q^2$ and give the difference between its two adjacent branches in closed form.

papers.title: Analytic Two-Loop Classical Bremsstrahlung Amplitude in Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We compute the leading long-wavelength term of the two-loop five-point amplitude for photon emission in the scattering of two massive spinless charges. Classical consistency suggests that two Coulomb exchanges dress the radiative tree amplitude. We show that this iteration accounts for the entire leading term and evaluate the resulting convolution. At fixed external transfer, the exchanges shift the momentum in the tree numerator, thereby changing the relative weights of its two polarization structures. We determine both coefficients at nonzero photon frequency and general relative velocity, with exact dependence on the spacetime dimension.

papers.title: Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization. II. Updated constraints and forecasts for the Simons Observatory and LiteBIRD
papers.abstract: We update the constraints on Lorentz-violating electrodynamics from the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Within the minimal Standard Model Extension, we consider the renormalizable CPT-odd and CPT-even operators of the photon sector, which source cosmic birefringence and circular polarization, respectively. Combining Planck, Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and South Pole Telescope (SPT) temperature and $E$-mode data with $B$-mode measurements from BICEP/Keck, SPT-3G D1 and SPTpol, we constrain the CPT-odd coefficients to $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|<7.75\times10^{-45}$ GeV and $|\mathbf{k_{AF}}|<3.82\times10^{-45}$ GeV at 95% credible level. These are the strongest bounds to date from any probe, and are driven by the SPT-3G D1 $B$-mode data. For the first time in this type of analysis, we also include the Planck PR4 $EB$ spectrum, which yields a mild preference for a non-zero $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|$. For the CPT-even coefficient, we find $k_{F,E+B}<5.99\times10^{-32}$. Including the latest circular polarization measurements from the Cosmology Large Angular Scale Surveyor (CLASS) tightens this bound by about 7%. This is the first time that CMB circular polarization data contribute to constraining this coefficient. Finally, we forecast the sensitivity of the Simons Observatory (SO) and LiteBIRD. With linear polarization only, the two experiments are complementary, with SO tightening the CPT-even bound by about 30% and LiteBIRD the CPT-odd ones by 40 to 45%. Exploiting the sensitivity to circular polarization provided by the non-idealities of its half-wave plate, LiteBIRD could also improve the CPT-even bound by more than an order of magnitude.

papers.title: Flavor-dependent quark-mass scaling and the fate of the strange-matter window in self-bound quark stars
papers.abstract: In the flavor-dependent QMDD model, self-bound $ud$ quark matter can be the ground state at vanishing pressure and convert into $uds$ matter through a first-order transition. So far the mass functional has used parameters $(a,C)$ common to all flavors; here we let the strange sector have its own coupling, $C_s=α\,C_{u,d}$, and map the response of the zero-pressure parameter space. The $e^0_{ud}=930\,$MeV boundary is independent of $α$ by construction, whereas increasing $α$ enlarges the self-bound $ud$ domain and pushes the $e^0_{ud}=e^0_{uds}$ line towards larger $a$. The causality boundary $c^0_s=c$ is almost frozen near $a\simeq5.5$. The competition closes the strange-matter window at \RA{$α_{\rm crit}\simeq1.136$}: above it every causal self-bound parametrization is $ud$ at zero pressure, so a first-order $ud\!\to\!uds$ transition must occur at higher pressure, though not necessarily inside a star, since the maximum mass may be reached below the transition density. The transition pressure and the energy-density jump grow monotonically with $α$, both scale \RB{approximately} with the available-volume fraction $q=1-κ$, and the Seidov onset-instability diagnostic stays below unity.

papers.title: Imprints of Non-local Top-Higgs Interaction on Loop Induced Higgs Processes
papers.abstract: A composite Higgs arising from an underlying strong sector generally has non-local interactions with the elementary sector, formulated in terms of momentum-dependent form factors. We construct the minimal Ball-Chiu-type vertices consistent with gauge-invariant non-local $\bar{t}th$ couplings containing Wilson lines, where recursive Ward-Takahashi identities connect the Yukawa interaction to higher-order contact interactions. For a symmetric monopole form factor motivated by lowest-resonance dominance, we compute the top-loop contributions to $gg \to h$ and $h \to γγ$ amplitudes in closed form, and demonstrate a logarithmically enhanced deviation from the Standard Model. Current measurements at the LHC exclude the characteristic new physics scale below 3.6 TeV at $2σ$, while future colliders could extend the sensitivity to approximately 8 TeV.

papers.title: Loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ at NLO+PS for LHC simulations: exact, fast scale and PDF event weights, theory uncertainties, and the limits of rescaled LO+PS
papers.abstract: We study loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ production with charged-lepton and neutrino $Z$ decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD matched to parton showers, using public software at $\sqrt{s}=13$ and 13.6 TeV. An exact loop-amplitude cache reduces event-generation time by a factor of 26 with 450 scale and PDF weights, while Born suppression improves boosted-event statistics without changing the weighted prediction. We present inclusive results for both channels and charged-lepton differential and STXS Stage 1.3 predictions with theory uncertainties. At 13.6 TeV, fixed-order top-quark mass-scheme variations transferred to NLO+PS dominate the statistically precise central-Higgs STXS bins for $p_\mathrm{T}^V\ge150$ GeV, reaching 32-50%. An inclusive $K$ factor does not reproduce the boosted and jet-dependent NLO+PS spectra of the tested LO+PS samples, and the differences depend strongly on the shower prescription. For specified CMS- and ATLAS-style vetoed sources at 13.6 TeV, we construct separate charged-lepton and neutrino corrections using ensembles of gradient-boosted classifiers, with calibration, target-theory variations and transfer uncertainties. Independent tests show substantial improvement over inclusive rescaling in most tested distributions, but not uniform closure. In charged-lepton calibration comparisons, the median STXS uncertainty from transported NLO scales and transfer terms is 17% for both the CMS- and ATLAS-style corrections, compared with LO scale uncertainties of 28% and 26% at fixed $K$. These comparisons do not include the complete target-theory budget. The corrections do not restore the depleted hard-recoil population; the highest ATLAS-style $p_\mathrm{T}^H$ bin stays below NLO+PS even at the upper edge of its band. The setup, reference results, and source- and channel-specific models support new NLO+PS generation and reuse of existing samples within stated limits.

papers.title: A Universal Axion in a Twin-QCD Sector
papers.abstract: Dark matter may consist of multiple components with distinct particle-physics origins. We investigate a scenario in which a universal axion couples to both visible and twin QCD, with twin baryons providing a possible dominant dark-matter component. The presence of a second strongly interacting sector can substantially enhance the axion mass while preserving its role in resolving the strong-CP problem, provided the physical vacuum angles are appropriately aligned. For a representative uniformly rescaled twin spectrum with a confinement scale five times that of ordinary QCD, the axion mass is enhanced by approximately a factor of 25. Using lattice-informed QCD results and a two-temperature description of the early universe, we investigate the cosmological evolution and relative abundances of the dark-sector components. In a representative conditional numerical benchmark, axions account for a small percentage of the observed dark matter, while twin baryons could constitute the remainder for a suitable primordial baryon asymmetry. We also examine the implications for additional relativistic species, strong-CP alignment, and the interactions of stable twin matter. Our results provide a quantitative framework for exploring mixed axion--twin-baryon dark matter and identify the particle-physics and cosmological conditions necessary for a viable realization, including constraints from the thermal history and formation of cosmic structure.

papers.title: Universal Mass Equation for Equal-Quantum Excited-States Sets~III
papers.abstract: Using our simple logarithmic Universal Mass Equation, we considered heavy non-$q\bar{q}$ meson states. PDG2026 reported a series of mesons with quantum numbers not allowed for standard $q\bar{q}$ states. Using LQCD predictions, we evaluated a scalar $0^{++}$ and tensor $2^{++}$ glueball series for which predictions are available. This approach allows us to predict heavy states that require future experimental studies. Additionally, we consider the possible misidentification of some meson states.

papers.title: Scalar inelastic scattering of pseudo-Majorana dark matter through a radion portal
